ECLYPSE / DOCUMENTATION

Set up Cloud–Edge scenarios in Python.

Define an infrastructure, describe your services, and choose a placement strategy. Run the scenario locally and inspect the report before moving to remote emulation.

Run your first scenario → Installation

Your first run

  1. Install ECLYPSE →
  2. Create your scenario →
  3. Run and inspect the report →

Start locally: no service implementation required.

WHAT YOU CONFIGURE

Start with three building blocks.

01 / INFRASTRUCTURE

Nodes, links and resources

Use a topology builder or add nodes and links yourself. Set CPU, RAM, storage, availability, latency and bandwidth through assets.

Define a topology → 02 / APPLICATION

Services and requirements

Describe services as a graph with resource requirements and communication links. Start from a reference application or create your own.

Describe your services → 03 / EXPERIMENT

Placement and evolution

Choose a placement strategy, a seed and a run length. Add update policies and events when your scenario needs changes over time.

Configure a run →

SCENARIO IDEAS

What would you like to investigate?

Illustrative modelling questions, not preconfigured benchmarks or measured results. Each requires its own topology, resource assumptions and metrics.

VIDEO ANALYTICS

Processing near the cameras

Model preprocessing and inference as services. How does placement change when edge capacity or link latency changes?

Vary
Service requirements, edge resources and link assets.
Inspect
Service placement and the resource and interaction metrics you enable.
Model resources →
INDUSTRIAL SENSING

An edge node becomes unavailable

Represent sensor processing and alerting as a service graph. What happens to deployment when an infrastructure node fails?

Vary
Node availability and the timing of failure events.
Inspect
Deployment changes across simulation steps.
Explore update policies →
VARIABLE DEMAND

Resource requirements grow

Represent a demand increase through changing service requirements. How do different placement strategies respond?

Vary
CPU and RAM requirements, available capacity and strategy.
Inspect
Placement and resource metrics across comparable runs.
Explore strategies and policies →
Looking for runnable examples? Browse the example guides →

AFTER A RUN

Inspect the report.
Change one assumption.

Query application, service and interaction frames. Keep the seed and configuration explicit when comparing scenarios.

Read and query results → 
report = sim.report
services = report.service()
applications = report.application()
interactions = report.frame("interaction")

Choose CSV, JSON or Parquet for storage, and a pandas or Polars report backend. Available columns depend on the metrics configured for your run.

CHOOSE HOW TO RUN

Model first. Implement services when needed.

LOCAL SIMULATION

Work with service graphs

Explore resource-aware deployment using abstract services, placement strategies and update policies. No service implementation is needed.

Start locally →
REMOTE EMULATION

Run implemented services

Provide service logic and execute it through Ray with MPI-style or REST-style communication. This requires additional runtime setup.
